solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

R061-01.notes: B: narrator helps count the closing shop's stock and discovers the back-page list of items lent out (a record of trust in borrowers). A wrong: store closes anyway; no persuasion. C wrong: trumpet is a cheap student model with stuck valves, and nothing is sold to the dealer. D wrong: no argument; narrator only asks why it matters.

R061-02.notes: D: 'He only wanted to know what had been there'; 'nobody was going to read the ledger' / 'I'll read it.' A wrong: 'Not to sell it'; dealer takes stock. B wrong: new owners take the cases; no list required. C wrong: no teaching motive stated.

R061-03.notes: A: 'Instead he opened the ledger... drew a neat stroke' contrasts with the expected laugh/dismissal. B wrong: no evidence of rudeness; expectation stems from trumpet's low value. C wrong: it was 'a cheap student model.' D wrong: the man's delay is explained by the man, not by this expectation.

R061-04.notes: C: he 'drew a neat stroke through' a line in the ledger = a line; 'crossed out' confirms. A (blow), B (caress), D (illness) are other senses of 'stroke' that don't fit drawing in a ledger.

R061-05.notes: D is stated directly: 'to play in his high school's spring concert.' A, B, C have no support (trumpet's dents are its own condition; no opening-day concert; no lessons).

R061-06.notes: B: list is of items that 'had gone out the door and not come back,' some thirty years old; only the trumpet is crossed out, so the rest were never returned. A wrong: Arno is meticulous; no hint he forgot. C wrong: trumpet was cheap with stuck valves. D wrong: entries date back decades and the narrator had not seen him write the line (pre-existing).

R061-07.notes: C: the remark credits borrowers' intentions despite decades of non-return; he simply thanks the returner. A wrong: no anger shown ('He did not look up' is reticence, not anger) - the most tempting trap. B wrong: no plan to demand anything; store is closing. D wrong: no regret expressed.

R061-08.notes: A: first-person narrator calls him 'my uncle Arno' and helps count during the final week. B wrong: Arno is referred to in third person. C wrong: the man is described from outside. D wrong: first-person 'I', no access to others' thoughts.

R061-09.notes: D: carrying the ledger himself and not offering it signals it is personal/precious to him. A wrong: overreads; the point is the ledger's meaning, not distrust of narrator generally (narrator was trusted to read stock counts). B wrong: dealer takes the stock, not the ledger; Arno keeps it. C wrong: no relief indicated.

flags.note: 'First see' is slightly loose: the narrator watched Arno open the ledger to the back page and strike a line ('found a line I had not seen him write') apparently while still on the ladder, before climbing down to look. A careful student could argue C. Suggest rewording the stem to 'first read the list' or 'first looked at the list for himself/herself' to tie it to 'I climbed down from the ladder and looked at the back page.'

R061-10.notes: B: 'Then he thanked the man, and the man left... I climbed down from the ladder and looked at the back page.' A wrong: list discovered on the fourth afternoon, and 'a line I had not seen him write' shows narrator hadn't seen it. C wrong-ish: narrator climbed down before looking (see flag). D wrong: the reading happened on the fourth day, before the last day.
